misconceptions.statement: The pupil collects data that does not answer the question being investigated.
The pupil organises data into categories that overlap, omit responses or do not preserve the original data.
The pupil counts symbols without applying the pictogram key.
The pupil reads a line graph without attending to ordered change over the horizontal variable.
The pupil treats a pie-chart sector as an isolated count instead of a part of the whole circle.
The pupil assumes the mean must be an observed value or confuses mean with the most common value.
The pupil reads a value without checking labels, units, scale or what the data represent.
The pupil expects a small random experiment to match the expected likelihood exactly.
The pupil uses possible, likely and certain as interchangeable descriptions.
